stanzas.loss_note: The translation flattens the colloquial emphasis of the particle 'to' in 'tumne to kaha tha' (which adds a layer of gentle accusation or contrast) and the specific nuance of 'yun hi' (just like this / effortlessly).

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The emotional pain of heartbreak, grief, or disappointment in love.
acceptable_visual_variants: A person sitting alone in a dimly lit room looking downcast
A stylized silhouette with a faint, glowing crack in the center of the chest
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: The physical heart shattered into pieces.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing a literal anatomical heart cracking or breaking like glass, which looks like a medical emergency or a horror scene rather than emotional grief.
metaphor_spans.tenor: The emotional state of grief and heartbreak.
metaphor_spans.vehicle: A physical object breaking or shattering.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a person looking downcast with a subtle, symbolic crack or shadow over their chest area, or focus on their sorrowful expression and posture.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: An immense, overwhelming volume of tears and grief.
acceptable_visual_variants: A person standing on a dark, vast shoreline looking out at a turbulent sea
A stylized illustration where tears flowing from a face merge into wavy, ocean-like blue lines
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: A literal ocean made entirely of tears.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting a literal person drowning in a massive body of blue water, which looks like a natural disaster or flood rather than a metaphor for crying.
metaphor_spans.tenor: An immense amount of crying and deep sorrow.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a person crying with tears that artistically blend into a vast, dark, wavy background pattern resembling water, or a solitary figure standing before a vast, dark ocean under a stormy sky.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of 'जो' (jo) as 'When' in 'When the heart broke' shifts the conditional/concessive nuance of 'जो दिल टूट गया' (even if/so what if the heart broke) to a purely temporal or situational one.

The emphatic particle 'तो' (to) in 'तुमने तो कहा था' (you, at least, had said / but you had said) is flattened in the translation, losing the subtle contrastive emphasis on the addressee's past assertion.

The colloquial idiomatic nuance of 'यूं ही' (yun hi - just like this, effortlessly, without change) is simplified to 'go on' in 'Life would go on', losing the specific flavor of continuity without effort or disruption.

annotation.theme: The painful contrast between a lover's past promises of continuity and the overwhelming reality of heartbreak.

original_poem:
क्या हुआ  
जो दिल टूट गया  
तुमने तो कहा था  
ज़िन्दगी यूं ही चलेगी  
आंसुओं का यह समंदर  
कभी थम न सकेगा  
क्या हुआ  
जो दिल टूट गया
translated_poem:
What happened  
When the heart broke  
You had said  
Life would go on  
This sea of tears  
Would never stop  
What happened  
When the heart broke
